spec.header: PRE-CHECK ON ALREADY-SCREENED DATA; NOT CONFIRMATION; E_up promoted post hoc
spec.question: Is lower Chung-Lu closure before E_up onset reducible to neighbourhood turnover + volume + age?

units.main: exp_3 concept_year_indicators.parquet; fold in {screen, reference}; age >= 0; 2005 <= year <= 2019; closure finite (reference rows have age = NaN in the file and therefore drop out)
units.mesh: exp_4 features.parquet; age >= 0; 2005 <= year <= 2019; aligned 'closure' finite

spec.deviation_D1: The plan lists MeSH 'beta_sim' as aligned. In features.parquet the column computed with the vendored main-pool code is 'beta_sim_raw' (Spearman/Pearson with plan-native 'beta_sim' only r = 0.16). SPEC P therefore uses beta_sim_raw in BOTH populations (like-for-like); plan-literal 'beta_sim' is run as sensitivity SPEC B_native. Declared before any statistic was computed.

step_2_1.demean: within concept, rows with both finite; concepts with >= 3 valid years

fit.main: OLS on fold=='screen' unit rows with complete covariates, applied to all rows with complete covariates
fit.mesh: OLS on all unit rows with complete covariates (label-blind), applied to all rows

specs.P: closure ~ 1 + new_rel + novelty + beta_sim(raw) + log1p(vol) + log1p(vol3) + age [+ H in main]  (PRIMARY)
specs.R: as P with beta_sim_rar replacing beta_sim(raw) (complete-case)
specs.V: closure ~ 1 + log1p(vol) + log1p(vol3) + age [+ H in main]  (reduced model of P: volume-only baseline)
specs.D_new_rel / D_novelty / D_beta_sim: closure ~ 1 + <one turnover variable> + log1p(vol) + log1p(vol3) + age (diagnostic)
specs.B_native: MeSH only: P with plan-native beta_sim replacing beta_sim_raw
specs.POS: closure ~ 1 + closure_raw + log1p(vol) + log1p(vol3) + age  (plan positive control)
specs.POS_ORACLE: closure ~ 1 + (closure + N(0, (0.1 sd)^2) noise, seed 0) + log1p(vol) + log1p(vol3) + age  (strict pipeline positive control: must erase the effect)
specs.NEG: closure ~ 1 + N(0,1) noise (seed 0) + log1p(vol) + log1p(vol3) + age  (negative control)
specs.V0: closure ~ 1 + log1p(vol) + log1p(vol3) + age  (reference for NEG: noise must retain ~100% of V0)

step_2_2.missing: event-study cells whose covariates are missing get NaN (never imputed); the treated-unit loss is reported and S_raw is recomputed on the SAME finite cells (S_raw_cc) as the retained-fraction denominator

step_2_3_gate.mesh: analysis.mainpool_es (exp_4), E_up matches from analysis_summary.json mainpool_block, B = 2000, fresh default_rng(42)
step_2_3_gate.pass: |S diff| < 1e-6 AND both CI endpoints within 0.02 of the recorded CI

step_2_4.bootstrap: resample treated units; ONE shared index set for raw and residualised (paired); main B = 1000 (seed as gate), MeSH B = 2000 (seed 42)
step_2_4.retained: S_res / S_raw_cc; paired-bootstrap percentile CI; replicates with |S_raw_cc_b| < 0.05 |S_raw_cc| dropped
step_2_4.mde: 2.8 x bootstrap SE; in SD units of the unit-level pooled SD of the outcome column

spec.step_2_5: fixed-effect IVW (w = 1/SE^2) of S_res across the two populations; Cochran Q (df = 1), p_Q, I^2 with Q-profile CI; same for S_raw (must reproduce side-by-side IVW -0.410, SE 0.125, Q 6.16). Q is underpowered at k = 2.

verdict_rule.NOT REDUCIBLE TO TURNOVER (seen data): S_res 95% CI excludes 0 AND retained lower CI >= 0.5
verdict_rule.LARGELY TURNOVER: S_res 95% CI covers 0 AND retained point estimate < 0.3
verdict_rule.applies_to: SPEC P per population; pooled verdict on S_ivw_res with the same rule (retained = S_ivw_res / S_ivw_raw_cc; retained CI for the pooled verdict from the IVW of paired bootstrap replicates)

control_pass_rules.POS: informative only: retained expected to shrink in proportion to the within-concept correlation of closure with closure_raw
control_pass_rules.NEG: S_NEG / S_V0 within [0.9, 1.1] in each population
control_pass_rules.PLACEBO: main only (exp_3 pseudo-onset design re-generated with rng 11): S_res CI covers 0

spec.bad_control_caveat: turnover may be part of the brokerage MECHANISM rather than a confounder; partialling it out then understates brokerage, so S_res is a conservative lower bound; S_fit = S_raw_cc - S_res and the single-covariate decompositions show which covariate carries the shared part.
